question.text: What is the minimum percentage of the AMC's net worth that a sponsor must contribute under SEBI Mutual Fund Regulations?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, the sponsor of a mutual fund is required to contribute a minimum of 40% to the net worth of the Asset Management Company. This minimum stake ensures the sponsor retains meaningful "skin in the game" and continues to bear primary responsibility for the AMC's sound operation, capital adequacy, and continuity. Sponsors holding below 40% of the AMC's net worth are treated as co-sponsors, subject to the same eligibility and fit-and-proper criteria. The Trap: 51% is a common corporate-law controlling-stake number but is not the regulatory floor for sponsor contribution. 26% is a Companies Act threshold for blocking special resolutions, not relevant here. 75% is far above the regulatory minimum. The exact figure prescribed for sponsor contribution to AMC net worth is 40%. Note: The cited pages of the NISM Series V-A Mutual Fund Distributors workbook (p.62-p.66) set out sponsor eligibility (positive net worth in each of the five immediately preceding years, positive liquid net worth above the proposed AMC capital contribution, net profit in each of the immediately preceding five years, and AMC net worth of not less than Rs. 50 crore) but do not state the 40% minimum sponsor contribution to AMC net worth. The framing above is general SEBI Mutual Fund Regulations knowledge.
